NIMBUS ANALYTICS — ENGINEERING ONBOARDING GUIDE
People Operations & Engineering Enablement
Effective February 12, 2024 | INTERNAL — ALL EMPLOYEES

OWNER: Tomás Aguirre, VP Engineering

WELCOME

Every engineering hire completes a 4-day onboarding bootcamp during their first week,
run twice a month by Engineering Enablement. By day 5 you should have shipped a small
change to production through the full pipeline.

FIRST-WEEK CHECKLIST

  Day 1: Laptop setup (managed image, disk encryption enforced), SSO enrollment with
         hardware security key, 1Password vault, Slack channels (#eng-announce,
         #helios-db, #incidents, #ship-it).
  Day 2: Clone the nimbus-core monorepo, run the local stack, pair with your
         onboarding buddy (assigned before your start date).
  Day 3: Bootcamp sessions — architecture tour: Skyhook (event ingestion pipeline),
         Prism (dashboard service), Gatekeeper (auth and production access broker),
         helios-db (primary Postgres cluster).
  Day 4: Ship your starter task through Skyship, our continuous-delivery system.
  Day 5: Retro with your manager; 30-60-90 plan agreed and written down.

HOW WE SHIP

  — Trunk-based development: short-lived branches, merged behind feature flags.
  — Skyship deploys on every green merge; production deploys freeze on Fridays.
  — Every service has a runbook; on-call is opt-in before your 90th day.

30-60-90 EXPECTATIONS

title: Nimbus Analytics — Information Security Policy v3
short_summary: Security policy v3: SSO with hardware keys, production access only via Gatekeeper (recorded sessions), quarterly access reviews, 24h offboarding revocation, data classification, 13-month customer data retention, 24h incident reporting.
excerpt:
NIMBUS ANALYTICS — INFORMATION SECURITY POLICY
Version 3.0 | January 25, 2024 | INTERNAL — ALL EMPLOYEES

OWNER: Security Team (CISO office) | Approved by: Priya Raghavan, CTO

SCOPE

Applies to all employees, contractors, and systems that touch Nimbus or customer
data. Annual security training is mandatory; completion is tracked by People Ops.

ACCESS CONTROL

  — Single sign-on with phishing-resistant hardware keys (YubiKey) is required for
    all internal systems. Passwords live only in the company 1Password vault.
  — Production access is brokered exclusively through Gatekeeper. Direct SSH to
    production hosts is prohibited; all sessions are recorded.
  — Access follows least privilege and is re-certified in quarterly access reviews.
    Offboarding must revoke all access within 24 hours of departure.

DATA CLASSIFICATION

  PUBLIC      Marketing material, published docs.
  INTERNAL    Default for company information (this policy, runbooks, wikis).
  RESTRICTED  Customer event data, compensation data, board and legal material.

Customer event data is retained for 13 months and then deleted from Skyhook and
helios-db backups on a rolling schedule. Restricted data may not be exported to
personal devices or unapproved SaaS tools.

ENDPOINTS AND VENDORS

  — Laptops run the managed image: full-disk encryption, screen lock, MDM agent.
  — New vendors require a security review and a signed DPA before any data flows.

INCIDENT REPORTING

excerpt:
NIMBUS ANALYTICS — ON-CALL RUNBOOK
Version 1.0 | November 2, 2023 | INTERNAL — ENGINEERING
STATUS NOTE: SUPERSEDED BY ON-CALL RUNBOOK v2.0 (APRIL 2024)

OWNER: Lena Fischer, Head of SRE

ROTATION

One primary and one secondary engineer per week, per service group (Skyhook,
Prism, helios-db). Handoff happens Mondays at 10:00 in #incidents. PagerBot,
our legacy Slack paging bot, delivers alerts to the primary.

ESCALATION (v1)

  1. Primary acknowledges the PagerBot alert. If no acknowledgement within
     15 minutes, PagerBot pages the secondary.
  2. If the incident is customer-visible and unresolved after 30 minutes,
     page Lena Fischer (Head of SRE) directly by phone.
  3. Executive notification is manual: the on-call engineer emails the CTO
     for anything affecting more than 10% of customers.

DATABASE FAILOVER (helios-db)

Failover to the standby replica is a MANUAL procedure documented in the
db-failover wiki page. Expected recovery time objective (RTO): 45 minutes,
including manual DNS switch, replica promotion, and connection-pool restart.
Only SRE members with Gatekeeper production grants may execute it.

SEVERITY

Incidents are informally classified as "minor" or "major" at the discretion
of the on-call engineer. Major incidents require a written summary in
#incidents within 48 hours.

KNOWN GAPS (ACKNOWLEDGED AT PUBLICATION)

title: Nimbus Analytics — Postmortem: helios-db Outage (March 4, 2024)
short_summary: Blameless postmortem PM-2024-03: 3h42m helios-db outage, root cause a schema migration lock exhausting the pgbouncer pool; 38% of customers affected, $214K SLA credits; action items delivered automated failover and Runbook v2.
excerpt:
NIMBUS ANALYTICS — INCIDENT POSTMORTEM PM-2024-03
helios-db Primary Outage — March 4, 2024
Published March 9, 2024 | INTERNAL — ALL EMPLOYEES | BLAMELESS

INCIDENT COMMANDER: Lena Fischer | SCRIBE: on-call secondary

SUMMARY

On March 4, 2024, the helios-db primary Postgres cluster was unavailable or
severely degraded for 3 hours 42 minutes (09:14–12:56 UTC). Dashboards (Prism)
served stale data and event ingestion (Skyhook) buffered to disk. Approximately
38% of customers experienced dashboard latency or query failures. No events were
lost; buffered ingestion replayed fully by 14:30 UTC.

CUSTOMER AND BUSINESS IMPACT

  — 246 of ~640 customers affected (38%).
  — SLA credits issued: $214,000 against Q1 revenue.
  — 3 enterprise prospects in active evaluation were affected; CS notified.

ROOT CAUSE

A schema migration shipped at 09:02 UTC took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the
events table. Long-running analytical queries queued behind the lock, exhausting
the pgbouncer connection pool within 12 minutes. Health checks then failed and
the API tier began timing out. Failover was NOT attempted for 68 minutes because
the documented procedure was manual (Runbook v1, RTO 45 minutes) and the on-call
engineer initially diagnosed the issue as an application bug.

WHAT WENT WELL / WHAT DIDN'T

title: Nimbus Analytics — Postmortem: helios-db Outage (March 4, 2024)
short_summary: Blameless postmortem PM-2024-03: 3h42m helios-db outage, root cause a schema migration lock exhausting the pgbouncer pool; 38% of customers affected, $214K SLA credits; action items delivered automated failover and Runbook v2.
excerpt:
WHAT WENT WELL / WHAT DIDN'T

  + Skyhook disk buffering prevented data loss.
  — Manual failover and a 15-minute paging acknowledgement window delayed response.
  — No incident-commander role: three engineers debugged, nobody owned comms.

ACTION ITEMS

  1. Automate helios-db failover (owner: SRE) — DONE, shipped April 2024;
     codified in On-Call Runbook v2 (RTO now 8 minutes).
  2. Migration review gate: any migration touching events requires SRE sign-off
     and lock-timeout settings — DONE.
  3. pgbouncer pool sizing and per-role limits — DONE.
  4. Adopt severity matrix and IC role — DONE (Runbook v2).

Source: sre/postmortems/PM-2024-03.md | Classification: INTERNAL

title: Nimbus Analytics — Performance Review Guide FY2024
short_summary: FY2024 review guide: April/October cycles, 5-level rating scale with 10/25/50/10/5 calibration guidance, peer feedback (3-5 peers), promotion windows; comp adjustments follow the manager-level compensation bands.
excerpt:
NIMBUS ANALYTICS — PERFORMANCE REVIEW GUIDE FY2024
People Operations | February 28, 2024 | INTERNAL — ALL EMPLOYEES

OWNER: Ingrid Solberg, VP People

CYCLE OVERVIEW

Nimbus runs two review cycles per year, closing in April and October. Each cycle
has four steps: self-review, peer feedback, manager narrative, and calibration.
Promotions are decided only inside these windows; off-cycle promotions require
exec approval.

RATINGS

Performance uses a 5-level scale: Redefines, Exceeds, Meets, Approaching, Below.
Calibration guidance (not a forced curve): roughly 10% Redefines, 25% Exceeds,
50% Meets, 10% Approaching, 5% Below across a calibrated population. Ratings are
calibrated in panels chaired by the department head with People Ops in the room.

PROCESS AND TIMELINE (APRIL CYCLE)

  Week 1    Self-review submitted (impact against your 30-60-90 or OKRs).
  Weeks 1-2 Peer feedback: each employee nominates 3–5 peers; managers may add.
  Week 3    Manager narrative drafted: evidence-based, examples over adjectives.
  Week 4    Calibration panels; ratings finalized; promotion cases decided.
  Week 5    Delivery conversations. Written summaries land in Workday.

COMPENSATION LINKAGE

title: Nimbus Analytics — SOC 2 Type II Audit Summary (2024)
short_summary: SOC 2 Type II (Jun 2023-Mar 2024, Hartley & Voss): zero major exceptions; two minor findings — offboarding revocation latency and a Prism log-retention gap — both remediated by Q3 FY2025. Next window opens July 2024.
excerpt:
NIMBUS ANALYTICS — SOC 2 TYPE II AUDIT SUMMARY
Security & Compliance | April 30, 2024 | RESTRICTED — MANAGERS AND ABOVE

OWNER: CISO office | Auditor: Hartley & Voss LLP

RESULT

Nimbus received a SOC 2 Type II report with ZERO major exceptions for the audit
window June 1, 2023 – March 31, 2024, covering the Security, Availability, and
Confidentiality trust criteria. Two minor findings were noted (below). The full
report is available to customers under NDA through the trust portal.

SCOPE

Systems in scope: Skyhook (ingestion), Prism (dashboards), Gatekeeper (access
broker), helios-db (primary datastore), corporate identity and endpoint
management. The March 4 helios-db outage was reviewed under Availability; the
auditor accepted the postmortem and remediation evidence (automated failover,
Runbook v2) as an effective corrective-action process.

MINOR FINDINGS

  F-1  Offboarding latency. 4 of 31 sampled departures had access-revocation
       tickets closed more than 5 business days after the departure date,
       against a 24-hour policy (Information Security Policy v3). Remediation:
       automated offboarding workflow triggered from the HRIS, due Q3 FY2025.
       Owner: IT + People Ops.

  F-2  Log retention gap. Prism service logs were retained 90 days in one
       region versus the documented 180-day standard. Remediation: retention
       policy unified in the logging pipeline, due Q3 FY2025. Owner: SRE.

NIMBUS ANALYTICS — PROJECT ALPINE: WORKFORCE CONTINGENCY MEMO
June 3, 2024 | RESTRICTED — EXECUTIVE TEAM ONLY | DO NOT FORWARD

PREPARED BY: Dana Whitfield (CEO), Ingrid Solberg (VP People), Marcus Bell (CFO)

STATUS

CONTINGENCY PLANNING ONLY. No reduction has been approved. This memo defines the
trigger, scope, and execution standards so that a decision, if ever taken, is
fast and humane. Distribution is limited to the executive team.

TRIGGER

If Q2 FY2025 net-new ARR misses plan by more than 25% (plan: $1.9M net-new),
the executive team convenes a decision gate on JULY 15, 2024. Absent that miss,
